label: As now
try: The Ground test, with a row counting as a column, as the rules always have. Two raiders come from the north and two from the east, the same distance away on screen. Press 3 to arm a Turret: its reach is drawn round it, twice as tall as it is wide. Enter places it. Then press s twice to start the battle, and watch how fast each raid comes.

label: Rows x2
try: The Ground test, with a row counting as two columns: a step up or down takes twice as long as one across. Press 3 to arm a Turret: its reach is as wide as it is tall on screen. Enter places it. Then press s twice to start the battle, and watch how fast each raid comes.

label: Sideways x2
try: The Ground test, with every number doubled across: up and down as now, across twice as far and twice as fast. Press 3 to arm a Turret: its reach is as tall as before and twice as wide. Enter places it. Then press s twice to start the battle, and watch how fast each raid comes.

label: Square tiles
try: The Ground test, with the rules as they always were and every tile drawn two columns wide, so a tile looks square. The eastern raid starts off the screen to the right: it now looks twice as far away as the northern one, because it is. Press 3 to arm a Turret and see its reach, Enter to place it, then s twice to start the battle, and watch how fast each raid comes: the eastern one has twice as far to go, on screen and in the rules.

label: PERIMETER, rows x2
try: PERIMETER's first round, its intro skipped, with a row counting as two columns: how a real level feels under it. Press 3 to arm a Turret and see its reach, Enter to place it, then s twice to start the battle, and watch the raid come over the ridge.
